page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c2d server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2926.98, placing it in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 23457.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 23685.51. Memory performance is notable, achieving a strong PassMark memory score of 2765.98, though memory bandwidth remains in the middle 50% for both small block cached reads at 1085.32 GB/sec and large block uncached reads at 80.47 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds of 301.82 tokens/sec on small LLM models, alongside average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations.

The c2d-highcpu-16 instance offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads due to its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high compute-to-memory ratio. However, the primary tradeoff is its low memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU and the complete absence of local SSD storage, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data caching. This configuration is best suited for compute-bound tasks such as web serving, software compilation, medium-scale batch processing, and lightweight machine learning inference.
